obligation: Segregate waste at source into four streams (wet, dry, sanitary, special-care) and hand it over to authorised waste pickers or collectors as the local body directs.
timeline: As directed by the local body from time to time
rule_2016_match: Rule 4(1)(a) (three streams: bio-degradable, non-biodegradable, domestic hazardous)

obligation: Wrap used sanitary waste (diapers, pads) securely in brand-owner pouches or suitable wrapping and put it in the separate sanitary-waste bin, not the wet, dry or special-care bins.
timeline: Whenever such waste is generated
rule_2016_match: Rule 4(1)(b) (earlier placed in the dry-waste bin)

obligation: Pay the user fee for solid waste management that the local body's bye-laws specify.
timeline: As per local body bye-laws

stakeholder: Large premises (hotels, restaurants, RWAs, market associations, gated communities, institutions above 5,000 sq m)
obligation: Ensure source segregation in partnership with the local body, provide separate collection streams, hand recyclables to authorised collectors or recyclers, process wet waste on premises by composting or bio-methanation as far as possible, and give residual waste to the local-body agency.
timeline: Within one year of Gazette notification of the Rules

obligation: Register on the centralised online portal with the concerned local body and report any change in registration details or conditions to it.
timeline: Portal-based; CPCB portal due within six months of commencement (Rule 16(1))

obligation: File an annual return on the centralised portal, including details of the Extended Bulk Waste Generator Responsibility (EBWGR) certificate for the total waste generated.
timeline: By 30 June every year

obligation: Obtain authorisation from the State Pollution Control Board for setting up and operating waste processing units.
timeline: Before operation; SPCB decides within 60 days (Rule 41(1)(v))

obligation: File quarterly returns and an annual return (Form III) with the local body covering waste received, waste processed, rejects sent to landfill and compost quality and sale; the data is published in the public domain.
timeline: Quarterly: by the 15th of the first month of the next quarter; annual: by 30 June

stakeholder: Local bodies, concessionaires and third parties in collection, segregation and transport
obligation: File quarterly and annual returns with the local body on quantities of wet, dry, sanitary and special-care waste handed to registered processors or recyclers; the local body validates them before further processing.
timeline: Quarterly: by the 15th of the first month of the next quarter; annual: by 30 June

obligation: Register with the local body, meet CPCB standards, send recyclable and non-recyclable fractions only to registered processors, and report waste received and dispatched through the portal.
timeline: Quarterly: by the 15th of the first month of the next quarter
rule_2016_match: Rule 15(h) (local bodies set up MRFs; no separate unit duty)

stakeholder: Industrial units using solid fuel near RDF / waste-based fuel plants
obligation: Replace part of solid-fuel use with refuse-derived fuel, segregated combustible fraction or agri-residue that meets CPCB norms (units within 100 km, row 1 of the Rule 11 table); register with the SPCB and file an annual return (Rule 11(2)).
timeline: At least 6% from commencement, 10% after 3 years, 15% after 6 years; annual return by 30 June

obligation: Register under the Rules and file an annual return in the prescribed form on the centralised portal stating the waste deposited.
timeline: By 30 June every year

obligation: Arrange door-to-door collection of segregated waste from all households including slums and informal settlements, and from commercial, institutional and other non-residential premises, directly or through a third party.
timeline: Ongoing

obligation: Frame bye-laws that incorporate the provisions of the Rules.
timeline: By 31 March 2027
rule_2016_match: Rule 15(e) (within one year of the 2016 notification)

obligation: Paint public bins green for wet waste and blue for dry waste; red bins for sanitary waste may be placed in public toilets where needed.
timeline: Ongoing
rule_2016_match: Rule 15(h) (green wet, white recyclable, black other)

obligation: Prepare a solid waste action plan in the prescribed format per the state policy, covering gram-panchayat-wise waste generation, a five-year projection, collection and transport planning and infrastructure mapping.
timeline: Within one year of notification of the state policy and strategy

obligation: Ensure that all local authorities comply with the Rules.
timeline: Ongoing; state master plans to be uploaded by 30 September 2026 (Rule 35(1)(xii))

obligation: Review local bodies' compliance on segregation, collection, sorting, processing, treatment and disposal, take remedial measures, and upload review-meeting minutes on the local body's portal.
timeline: At least once every quarter

stakeholder: State Pollution Control Boards / Pollution Control Committees
obligation: Enforce the Rules through local bodies and review their implementation in close coordination with the state urban and rural development departments.
timeline: At least twice a year

obligation: Establish the centralised online portal for registration of regulated entities and filing of annual returns, with national, state and district dashboards in the public domain.
timeline: Within six months of commencement of the Rules (in force 1 April 2026)
